name: ClaudeBot
follows_en: Yes, it follows robots.txt and Crawl-delay

ips.note: Anthropic's article says its robots respect "do not crawl" signals in robots.txt and will not try to bypass CAPTCHAs. It supports the non-standard Crawl-delay directive, for example `User-agent: ClaudeBot` followed by `Crawl-delay: 1`. It also says that blocking by IP address may not give a lasting opt-out, because it stops the robot from reading robots.txt. Anthropic's article states that robots.txt must be set for every subdomain you want to opt out.

vendor_quote: ClaudeBot helps enhance the utility and safety of our generative AI models by collecting web content that could potentially contribute to their training. When a site restricts ClaudeBot access, it signals that the site's future materials should be excluded from our AI model training datasets.

vendor_quote_source.title: Anthropic Help Center: Does Anthropic crawl data from the web, and how can site owners block the crawler? (7 April 2026)

what_en:
Anthropic names three robots in its help article: ClaudeBot for training data, [Claude-User](/bots/claude-user) for pages fetched at a user's request, and [Claude-SearchBot](/bots/claude-searchbot) for search quality. ClaudeBot is the training one. The article is dated 7 April 2026.

| Fact | ClaudeBot |
| --- | --- |
| Operator | Anthropic |
| Job | Training |
| robots.txt token | `ClaudeBot` |
| Follows robots.txt | Yes, it follows robots.txt and Crawl-delay |
| Published address list | Anthropic points to a list but advises against IP blocking |
| Vendor page read | 21 October 2026 |
block_en: Anthropic says a restriction signals that the site's future materials should be excluded from its training datasets. The wording says "future materials"; it does not say what happens to content already collected. The other two Claude robots are separate, so blocking ClaudeBot leaves their rules untouched.
compare_en: A separate search robot: blocking ClaudeBot does not touch it.

sources.title: Anthropic Help Center: Does Anthropic crawl data from the web, and how can site owners block the crawler? (7 April 2026)

answer_en: ClaudeBot is Anthropic's crawler for content that could contribute to model training. A robots.txt Disallow signals that a site's future materials should be excluded from training datasets. Anthropic honours Crawl-delay, and warns that blocking its IP addresses can stop it reading robots.txt, so use robots.txt instead.
